topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and sets out the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and sources of mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through accumulated mutations and microenvironmental support resulting from both intrinsic cellular processes and external pressures.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures and geographic population differences influence cancer incidence and public perceptions of risk.

topics.label: Pathogen-driven carcinogenesis and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote malignant transformation, using the geographic and molecular epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Molecular mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, UV radiation, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce specific DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and the initiator-promoter model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic promoters that drive chronic inflammation and cell proliferation from direct tumor-initiating mutagens.

topics.label: Host cell susceptibility and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how developmental timing and tissue context influence mutagen susceptibility before summarizing the discussed mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine the carcinogenicity of substances.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding subtopic summarises the lecture themes and reflects on the daily risk-benefit assessments surrounding carcinogen exposure.
